summary: The Android render closely matches React in typography, field dimensions, spacing, alignment, colors, corner radii, and error-state treatment.
No missing, clipped, or shifted elements are apparent; both sides show identical labels, values, helper text, red error outline, and error message.
Remaining differences are limited to subtle text and rounded-border antialiasing, without meaningful layout or component-bound drift.
likelyCauses: Platform-specific font rasterization and antialiasing.
Independent device-pixel rounding of strokes and rounded-corner curves.
cases.suggestedOwner: Design systems and Android UI engineering
suggestedFixes: Normalize font family, weight, size, and line-height tokens across React and Android.
Use identical border width and corner-radius values and snap component bounds to the same pixel grid.
Accept the current 97.13% pixel-perfect and 98.8% RGB similarity unless subpixel rendering parity is required.

summary: The React textarea has a dark charcoal outline, while the Android textarea uses a bright red outline, indicating inconsistent invalid/error-state styling.
React shows a gray diagonal resize handle at the textarea's lower-right corner; Android has no resize handle.
The "57 / 40" counter and "Agreement body must be shorter." message share one row in React, while Android stacks the counter above the message with larger vertical gaps.
likelyCauses: The Android and React implementations map error-state border colors differently.
The resize affordance is implemented only in the React textarea.
The platforms use different footer layout, element ordering, or margin rules for the counter and validation message.
cases.suggestedOwner: Cross-platform Textarea component and design-system team
suggestedFixes: Apply a shared invalid/error border token and stroke width in both implementations; make React red if the Android treatment is the intended error state.
Add an equivalent resize affordance to Android or explicitly disable resizing in both platforms.
Use a shared footer layout so the counter and validation message have the same order, baseline, and spacing on React and Android.
Normalize the vertical gap between the textarea bottom and the counter/message footer.

summary: Android status-dot fills are darker and more saturated than React across the green, orange, gray, and cyan states; React uses lighter, pastel-like fills.
Android outlines appear slightly thicker or darker, reducing the visible fill area while keeping the outer dimensions nearly unchanged.
Dot order, spacing, alignment, typography, and the 342×92 component bounds match. No elements are missing, clipped, or offset.
likelyCauses: Different semantic color-token mappings between React and Android.
A heavier native stroke width than the React CSS border.
Minor platform-specific antialiasing around the dark outlines.
suggestedFixes: Map Android status-dot fill tokens to the approved React palette, or explicitly approve and document the alternate palette.
Align the Android stroke width with the React border width and verify that corner radii remain equivalent.
Keep the current dimensions and spacing, then rerun the visual comparison after updating color and stroke tokens.

summary: React shows a thick, dark rectangular focus/selection outline around the full search-input row; Android renders the same row without that outline.
The missing Android outline leaves the search field bounded only by surrounding separators, so its active state is not visually indicated.
likelyCauses: Android may be rendering the unfocused/default search-field state while React is rendering the focused or selected state.
The active-border color and thickness may not be implemented or exposed by the Android search-field component.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android UI component owner for the selection popover and search field
suggestedFixes: Add the React-equivalent active-state border to the Android search row, including its top, sides, and bottom.
Align focus/selection state defaults and test-harness focus behavior so both platforms capture the same state.
Use the shared popover border color and thickness tokens instead of a native or default Android field style.

summary: The Android populated select has a roughly twice-as-heavy black outline as the React version, while its outer bounds and content alignment remain essentially unchanged.
The Android disabled select also has a slightly heavier light-gray outline than the React disabled border.
Typography, label and chevron placement, spacing, and component sizes match; no elements are missing or clipped.
likelyCauses: Android may use a 2 dp/px select stroke where React uses a 1 px border.
Android density scaling may rasterize a nominal 1 dp border as multiple physical pixels.
Enabled and disabled outlines may use separate Android stroke-width tokens.
suggestedFixes: Match the Android select outline to the React stroke width, approximately 1 px/1 dp in the rendered comparison, for both populated and disabled states.
Keep the existing outer component bounds; adjust stroke weight rather than control size or padding.
Use explicit shared state colors and border tokens: black for the populated outline and the same light gray for the disabled outline.
intentional: The yellow top-right badge changes from “REACT” to “ANDROID,” including the badge width needed for the platform label.

summary: No actionable visual defects are apparent; typography, spacing, alignment, colors, shapes, bounds, and clipping closely match at the shared 390×844 viewport.
The recorded 1.33% pixel mismatch is below the configured 2% tolerance.
likelyCauses: Minor platform-specific text and icon rendering differences account for the remaining pixel variance.
suggestedFixes: No visual change is required; continue regression testing within the configured pixel tolerance.
intentional: Android shows a left-facing back arrow where React shows an X/close icon, reflecting Android's single combined forward flow versus React's two-step flow; these controls should remain platform-specific.

summary: Component bounds differ: React fills the 390×844 viewport edge-to-edge, while Android uses a smaller centered rounded modal over a dark gray scrim.
Headers differ: React shows “Settings” plus the “Channel #design” subtitle; Android shows only “Edit Channel” and omits the subtitle.
Pin controls differ: React has a “Preferences” heading, helper copy, and an off-state switch; Android omits these and shows a full-width outlined “Pin” action button.
Android omits the “Channel actions” heading and helper text. Its Name and Description fields are shorter, with heavier outlines; React's focused Name field has a double-ring treatment.
Cancel and Save differ in placement and state: Android places them below the fields with a disabled gray Save, while React places them at the bottom right with an active pink Save.
likelyCauses: The Android implementation uses a dialog component rather than React's full-screen panel component.
The Android feature specification omits or restructures the Preferences and Channel actions sections.
Component sizing and border-stroke tokens differ between the React and Android implementations.
Form state differs: Save is disabled and the Name field is not focused in the Android capture.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android channel-settings feature owner and design-system team
suggestedFixes: Use a full-screen 390×844 white panel on Android, removing the centered modal bounds, rounded outer corners, and dark scrim.
Match the React header by showing “Settings” and the “Channel #design” subtitle.
Restore the Preferences and Channel actions headings and helper copy; replace the standalone Pin button with the off-state switch.
Match React's field heights, border weight, corner radius, and focused Name-field outline, especially the taller Description textarea.
Move Cancel and Save into a bottom-right action area with the baseline divider, and reconcile Save's enabled state so visual state matches the actual form validity.

summary: React has a white header with a back arrow and inset gray divider; Android has a full-width yellow header, no back arrow, and the title aligned near the left edge.
React list labels are larger and bolder, with larger gray icons; Android labels and icons are smaller, lighter, and more compact.
Android content uses less left padding, a narrower icon-to-label gap, and substantially tighter vertical spacing than React.
Android adds Mobile, Storage, Applications, and Computers, while React adds a second Notifications item and a Documentation row with an external-link arrow.
The section heading differs: React shows On Raft Design, while Android shows On Visual Server; Android section headings are also lighter gray.
likelyCauses: Android is using a native-style toolbar instead of the shared React header component.
Typography, icon-size, padding, and row-density tokens are not shared across platforms.
The platform implementations source different settings navigation items or feature flags.
The external-link indicator is not implemented in the Android row component.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android UI and cross-platform design-system owner
suggestedFixes: Align the Android header with the React baseline: white background, back affordance, title placement, and divider bounds; alternatively define an explicitly approved platform-specific header variant.
Apply the baseline label typography and icon sizing, or update both implementations to use matching shared typography and icon tokens.
Normalize section and row padding, icon-to-label gaps, and vertical spacing to match the React spacing scale.
Reconcile the navigation manifests so both platforms show the same intended sections and items, including resolving Mobile, Storage, Applications, Computers, and the second Notifications entry.
Rename On Visual Server to On Raft Design if required by the baseline, and restore the Documentation row's external-link arrow on Android.

summary: The Android app bar truncates the title as “Computer Missing Pr...” and adds an outlined chat action; React shows the full title without that action.
The Chat and Reminder tabs use different icons on each platform: React uses a speech bubble and alarm clock, while Android uses a rectangular chat bubble and bell.

In the profile summary, React includes edit pencils for the name and description, uses a terminal-style Codex CLI icon, and displays a clipped “Capturing deterministic profile sta...” status; Android omits the pencils, uses a chip-like icon, and shows a compact “Working” status.
Android adds a Display name field above the description. Its description body text is smaller and wraps to two lines, while React's larger text wraps to three lines and has an edit pencil.

Info and Runtime sections differ in structure: Android adds a computer-value dash, shows Created and Creator side by side, uses a letter avatar, lays out Runtime Config in two columns, and reveals Environment Variables and Created Agents that are not visible in React.
likelyCauses: The Android profile screen uses a different component schema and field-visibility configuration from React.
Separate responsive breakpoint rules are producing different stacks, columns, typography, and vertical spacing.
Platform-specific icon and avatar mappings have diverged between implementations.
The Android app-bar action row includes an extra button, reducing the title's available width.
Status and profile-edit affordances are rendered by different components rather than a shared specification.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android UI team with the shared design-system owner
suggestedFixes: Align the app bar with React by matching action icons, title width, and truncation behavior; either remove the Android chat action or add the corresponding React action.
Use the same Chat, Reminder, Codex CLI, role, and status icon set on both platforms.
Match profile and description edit affordances, including showing the same pencils and allowing the complete status text to fit without clipping.

Unify the displayed fields and ordering by deciding whether Display name, the computer dash, Environment Variables, and Created Agents belong in the mobile profile view, then render them consistently.

Standardize mobile typography and layout: use matching description sizing and consistent single-column or two-column arrangements for Info and Runtime Config, including equivalent creator avatar rendering.

summary: Android renders the header and large profile avatars as lavender tiles with a black "A", while React uses person-outline glyphs.
React includes an outlined "(you)" badge beside the handle and a person detail on the top-right chat icon; Android omits both and shows a plain speech bubble.
The Description section diverges: React shows "Owner" and a heading-aligned pencil, while Android shows "Product design and server administration." with no pencil.
The Role row differs: React has a circled question-mark icon and an "Owner" pill; Android has a circled information icon plus pencil and a "Member" pill.

Created Agents differs in state and bounds: React shows count 0 and an empty-state message, while Android shows count 2 and a rounded outlined card containing Product UX / Claude Code and Release Notes / Codex CLI rows, cyan-black icons, and green and gray status squares.
likelyCauses: Android is using an initials-based avatar fallback instead of the shared profile icon.
Android has not implemented the same conditional "(you)" badge and header icon composition.
The platforms are rendering different member fixtures or API fields for description and role.
Role iconography is mapped differently between the React and Android implementations.
Created Agents is using different seed data or query state across platforms.
cases.suggestedOwner: Android member-profile feature team, with shared design-system and fixture/API owners as needed
suggestedFixes: Replace the "A" avatar fallback in both avatar locations with the shared person-outline glyph while retaining the current tile size and color.
Add the outlined "(you)" badge beside the handle and restore the person detail on the header chat icon.
Align the Description value and edit-pencil presence and placement with the intended baseline.
Use consistent Role iconography and ensure the role pill reflects the same member role on both platforms.
Use a common Created Agents fixture or explicitly match the count, empty state versus populated card, row content, icons, and status colors.
